_note: B-66. macOS and Linux levers through the bash runtime (runtime "bash": a vetted script from levers/bash/scripts, pinned by hash in levers/bash/manifest.json, run by core/levers/bridge.py BashBridge). Mock only: the scripts read and change synthetic host files under levers/bash/mock; no systemctl, launchctl or real host is touched.

levers.name: unix.disk-usage
levers.description: Report used space per mount of the client's one macOS or Linux host and which mounts are over a threshold. Read only. Mock host data.

threshold_pct.description: Flag mounts at or above this percent used (default 80)

levers.name: unix.restart-service
levers.description: Restart one allowlisted service (cups, chronyd or rsyslog) on the client's macOS or Linux host. Mock of a service manager restart: bumps a counter in the client's own host state. A dry-run (--what-if) returns the same diff and changes nothing.

service.description: The service to restart; only these three names exist

impact.L1: A person whose printing, clock or logging stalled gets it back; a restart briefly interrupts that one service for whoever is using it.
impact.L2: The client's host is repaired the same day without a visit; restarting at the wrong hour can interrupt printing or log collection during a busy period.
impact.L3: A known fix is one approved, audited button instead of a remote shell session, and the allowlist keeps anything else from being restarted.
impact.L4: Mac and Linux users get the same safe automation as Windows users, with no free-form shell for a fooled model to reach.

levers.name: unix.clear-cache
levers.description: Delete the plain files in one allowlisted cache folder (user-cache or app-cache) of the client's macOS or Linux host. Mock host files. A dry-run (--what-if) lists exactly the files that would go and deletes nothing.

scope.description: Which cache folder to clear; only these two exist

impact.L1: A person with a full disk or a stale cache gets space and fresh data back; the first open of some apps is slower while the cache is rebuilt.
impact.L2: The client avoids a disk-full outage on a Mac or Linux workstation; clearing during work hours can slow an app that is rebuilding its cache.
impact.L3: The deletion is a listed, approved and audited set of named files, so the MSP can show exactly what was removed and when.
impact.L4: Cache files are disposable by definition and rebuilt by the application; folders, links and odd names are never touched.
